hypothesis: If Darwin's erosion-rate argument holds, the time since the late Chalk (latest Cretaceous) is of order 300 million years, i.e. between 250 and 350 Ma.
pass_criterion: The numeric age of the top of the Cretaceous (the Cretaceous–Paleogene boundary) on the International Chronostratigraphic Chart lies between 250 and 350 Ma.
fail_criterion: The age of the top of the Cretaceous is below 250 Ma or above 350 Ma. The chart gives about 66 Ma, which would be a refutation.
interpretation: 'Latter part of the Secondary period' is read as the late Chalk, the Late Cretaceous, ending at the K–Pg boundary. 'Secondary' corresponds to the Mesozoic. The test compares Darwin's implied elapsed time with the chart's radiometrically calibrated boundary age. It tests the conclusion about elapsed time, not his erosion arithmetic.

dataset.name: International Chronostratigraphic Chart
dataset.why_it_fits: The chart is the standard reference for numeric ages of stage and system boundaries. The fields used are the boundary age in Ma for the top of the Cretaceous and the base of the Upper Cretaceous.
